title: Correct HTTP/2 load-client session rollover and pre-handoff outcomes
description: Batch validation exposed that the synthetic network load client kept using one closed HTTP/2 session, producing constructor failures before new requests could reach the gate. Replace retired sessions only for future offers without retrying/replaying existing IDs. Classify proven pre-stream rejection as not-sent, preserve Unknown after accepted stream handoff, record session/GOAWAY/status diagnostics, drain all existing observers and clean up all sessions. Use direct red-before-fix fixtures and rerun network cohorts; preserve historical single-session datasets and their limitations. Production batching/transport protocol remains unchanged.
notes: Corrected benchmark client lifecycle without production changes. Future offers replace retired HTTP2 sessions; existing IDs are never replayed. Issued starts after request/stream construction; rejected pre-stream construction is NotSent and unavailable post-handoff results are Unknown. Session, GOAWAY, reset, error and status counters plus complete cleanup added. Four fixtures pass; two original regressions ran red before correction. Independent review passed. Corrected 30-run network matrix reconciled; historical single-session probes are preserved.
close_reason: Client rollover/accounting fixed, direct regressions green, reviewed and exercised by corrected network matrix.

title: Implement batched writes and synchronized group completion
description: Operator explicitly requires batching after the per-record synchronization measurements. Implement explicit native content batches and bounded automatic group commit for synchronized native/HTTP/gRPC calls. Preserve the written single-call fast path, record/property format, per-record metadata and immutable history. Return success after the selected shared write/sync boundary; preserve owned input and correct failed/unknown outcomes on admission/I/O/worker failures. No new dependency or power-loss subsystem. Validate direct I/O/lifecycle invariants and benchmark batch-size, concurrency, throughput and tails against versioned baselines.
notes: Implemented bounded synchronized group commit and append_batch with per-item results, unchanged frame/hash/schema and the caller-thread Written fast path. 55 runtime tests and 3 compile-fail doctests pass; live Python/Node checks cover both completions. Independent design, source, test and numeric reviews complete. Published 75 native release runs and 30 corrected network runs; 42 historical single-session probes are labelled and retained. Native synchronized groups of 1,024 records reached median 189,975.470/s versus 204.598/s for the current single-record reference (~929x), with whole-call p99 ~8.87ms. Failure, unknown and not-sent populations plus exact receipts/IDs reconcile. No new dependency, per-event default barrier, archive or power-loss subsystem. Benchmark session bug fixed under deleuze-2aa. Results: papers/measurements/2026-10-23-batched.
close_reason: Batched writes and shared synchronized completion implemented, tested, independently reviewed and measured; current API/guides and reproducible results complete.

title: Measure native and network capture performance with complete workload accounting
description: Build dependency-free benchmark utilities for native append versus a frame-sized std-file baseline, and real HTTP/gRPC fixed-rate load. Report storage boundary, offered/issued/not-sent work, client and server retained/failed/unknown populations, drain, throughput, bytes and actual/scheduled tail latency. Validate IDs and exact retained payloads after timing. Run a modest release-mode local matrix with hardware/runtime/storage details and explicit same-host/client limitations. No power-loss work, deployment-nines claim, automatic dependency adoption or premature production optimization. Commit and push coherent steps frequently.
notes: Completed dependency-free native/file-floor and real HTTP/gRPC measurement utilities, raw TSV samples, exact ID/receipt/pattern reconciliation and reproducible randomized release matrices. 72 baseline plus 24 gate-capacity runs completed with zero unknown/pending/partial outcomes; known server rejections and client not-sent work remain visible. Independent design, source and report reviews completed. Native 128-byte one-producer written median 593,519.651/s, per-run p99 median 3,750ns; local synchronized median 238.227/s. Capacity 256 eliminated observed server rejection but moved work to client cap and raised tails without materially improving useful rate. Seven native/shared helper tests and three shared gate-example tests, real protocol/cap fixtures, fmt and Clippy pass. Data/report at papers/measurements/2026-10-23; full raw artifacts ignored under target/measurements. No production path/default/dependency changes or deployment-nines claim. Frequent commits/pushes completed; follow-up profiling/batching in deleuze-77u.
close_reason: 96 release runs, exact reconciliation, independent review, reproducible harnesses and published local report/datasets complete; profiling/batching tracked separately.

title: Implement bundled HTTP and gRPC capture gates
description: Optional HTTP and raw-content unary gRPC gates over public Log::append, with shared receipts, bounded owned acquisition, cancellation-safe storage ownership, close/drain lifecycle and in-memory request outcomes. Python and Node clients support both protocols; custom adapter and operation guides document semantics and limits. Tokio/Axum plus standard http-body/tower-service traits were discussed and accepted. No request archive, alternate writer, protobuf wrapper or power-loss subsystem.
notes: Implemented, independently reviewed and validated. Six gate fidelity regressions plus two client regressions ran red before fixes and now pass. All-feature validation: 39 Rust runtime tests and 3 compile-fail doctests pass; native-only validation: 20 runtime tests pass. Live Python/Node HTTP and gRPC checks pass for exact native content, receipts and populations. Formatting and Clippy with warnings denied pass. Coherent commits pushed repeatedly per operator preference. No throughput/nines claim; lower-parser coverage and offered-load measurement continue under deleuze-5n0.
close_reason: Optional HTTP/gRPC gates, two-language clients, lifecycle/failure tests, independent review and live interoperability checks complete and pushed incrementally.

title: Implement the first native capture core and shared adapter surface
description: Operator said send it after approving the record profile. Complete concrete design/plan review, then build a useful standalone Rust core: gate packing of ordinary content, writer-owned seq/hash/timestamps, binary persistence/recovery and one public ingestion surface. Prepare bundled HTTP/gRPC gates and custom adapter guide through that same surface. Dependency choices must be discussed per AGENTS.md before adoption. Producers mask; ABAC-aware reference assistance does not rewrite data. Preserve privacy and contents-only rules.
notes: Implemented first native crate after independent reduced design, plan and source reviews. One append file, ordinary I/O/clean reopen, private seq/hash/write times, owned packing, immutable records, independent read snapshots and result-bounded linear pages. Official BLAKE3 1.8.7 sole direct dependency. Passed20 tests+3 compilefail doctests, fmt and Clippy with warnings denied. No performance/nines claim. Custom adapter guide and concrete network proposal prepared; HTTP/gRPC implementation tracked in deleuze-qb2 and optional profiles in deleuze-89i. Network dependency discussion pending; not adopted. No power-loss machinery. License unset and publish=false.
close_reason: Reviewed native core and shared public adapter surface implemented and validated; bundled network gates and optional profiles tracked separately.

close_reason: Private acquisitions/context and original issue history preserved outside checkout; identifying catalogs, notes, provenance and tools removed. Current issue database rebuilt from sanitized state. Reachable Git history rewritten, identity/path scan passed and clean history published using a force-with-lease update. Public literature and generic design retained. Repository policy and future CLI logging now enforce the boundary.

title: Define and pressure-test the gate capture and performance contract
description: Develop and pressure-test the capture contract using public literature and generic reasoning. Capture every gate arrival, including retries and full/failing-gate arrivals, extremely quickly at deployment-funded reliability. Compare ownership, completion, overload, ordering and recovery. No dependency adoption without operator discussion. See design/starting-point.md.
notes: Native/gate capture and performance contracts are implemented and reviewed. The versioned baseline under deleuze-tfo is followed by batched-sync implementation and 75 native plus 30 corrected network runs under deleuze-77u. Client reply uncertainty remains separate from server retention: 768 synchronized records survived overloaded gRPC reply loss. Failed/full arrivals stay in the population; generator not-sent work is shown separately. No deployment nines or maximum network capacity proven. Pre-Service parser observation coverage and sustained-load deployment budgeting remain open. Power-loss resilience remains outside the current build.

description: Continue the public literature study and generic synthesis. Preserve exact public-source provenance and reading depth. Private sources may inspire reasoning but all identifying material stays outside the repository.

title: Profile remaining packing and network handoff costs after batching
description: Use the reviewed batched-sync dataset and exact completion/population contracts. Compare per-record allocation/encoding/hash, writer dispatch and native/network handoff costs using controlled same-host builds and measurements before selecting changes. Explicit bulk Sync1024 median190k/s versus file213k/s; automatic64 native callers10.4k/s and synchronized network limits still differ. Written rates varied for both log and file floor across unisolated periods, so do not infer regression causality without A/B controls. Preserve properties/metadata authority and all arrivals; review any implementation plan and discuss new dependencies. No power-loss or novel cryptographic protocol work.

title: Add configurable record profile extensions
description: Implement the approved optional feature direction with explicit defaults: event types off, producer IDs off, possible Deleuze received_at off, producer-masked references passive with automatic assistance off until configured. Only Deleuze assigns authoritative record times; producer times stay properties. Any ABAC reference assistance leaves stored properties/metadata unchanged and never redacts on ingest. Concrete extension format and mapping design still required; first native core intentionally implements only seq/property_hash/created_at.

title: Resolve remaining source-discovery gaps
description: Continue source discovery outside the repository. Do not record private source identities, paths, catalogs, provenance or source-specific findings here. Only generic lessons may inform public design notes.
